title: NASA Changed Its Moon Mission. Here's Why.
rationale: A is literally true (NASA 2026-02-27, 2026-08-05, 2026-10-23) and its cover subject - the Moon, in a real NASA photo from Artemis II (art002e009289) - is frame 1 of the video, so cover, title and first 3 s match. It fits the Orbital Atlas cover style (dramatic real imagery from space, big uppercase white/yellow text) better than a high-bay hardware photo. Risk: the photo is from Artemis II, not Artemis III; the frame carries the label 'ARTEMIS II PHOTO' and the VO says 'was supposed to land here', never that Artemis III took it. B is NEXORA's former choice A (boosters), demoted because the cleared photo is portrait 1280x1920 and needs the ~orig file for a 16:9 1080p crop. C leads with an illustration. Which earns more clicks is a hypothesis for A/B, not a forecast.

concepts.title: NASA Changed Its Moon Mission. Here's Why.
concepts.visual_promise: the Moon up close (real Artemis II photo) and why the next crew stays in Earth orbit instead
concepts.main_subject: the Moon - lunar surface photographed from Orion on Artemis II
concepts.cover_asset: a2-lunar-surface (NASA, art002e009289); yellow 'ARTEMIS III' tag top-left, 'NO MOON LANDING' white, thin red strike line; no crew, no NASA insignia
concepts.hook_15s: 0-3 s: lunar surface photo (Artemis II, labelled), fast push-in, 'THE PLAN: LAND HERE'. VO: 'NASA's next Moon mission was supposed to land here.' 3-7 s: hard cut, diagram zooms out from Moon to Earth, LEO ring lights: 'NOW: 273 MILES UP'. VO: 'Now it won't even leave Earth orbit.' 7-11 s: Artemis II Earthset photo. VO: 'In April, four astronauts flew around the Moon on Artemis Two.' 11-15 s: SLS diagram, upper stage slides out. VO: 'And the next crew's rocket won't even carry the stage that sends Orion toward the Moon.'
facts: Artemis II flew around the Moon, flyby 2026-04-06 (NASA)
2026-02-27: Artemis III becomes a 2027 low-Earth-orbit test, landing moves to Artemis IV 2028 (NASA 2026-02-27, 2026-08-05)
Blue Moon test article orbit ~273 mi (NASA 2026-10-23)
Artemis III SLS flies a non-propulsive spacer instead of the ICPS (NASA 2026-08-05)
